# Configure auto-instrumentation

Configure Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric proxies to generate OpenTelemetry spans
for AI model and Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool calls. When you finish,
supported calls produce correlated network and payload spans in your trace
backend, with no tracing SDK in your applications.

@include '../../../global/partials/alerts/beta.mdx'

To learn how auto-instrumentation works, refer to
[Auto-instrumentation](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/auto-instrumentation).

## Requirements

- Consul Enterprise with a valid license for external processing, registered
  services, and configured mesh connectivity.
- The `consul-ai` [feature gate](/consul/docs/manage/feature-gates) enabled. On
  Kubernetes, set the `ai.enabled` Helm value to `true`.
- The AI Inference Gateway and MCP sidecar deployed for the model and tool
  traffic you want to observe.
- Agent, inference, and tool calls routed through the configured sidecar
  upstreams or gateways, on HTTP-aware listeners.
- An OpenTelemetry Collector and a trace backend reachable from the proxies and
  processors.
- An entry point that establishes trace context and a sampling decision for
  each request. Without a sampled `traceparent`, payload spans can be missing.
- Applications that forward trace context on downstream calls. Refer to [Trace
  context
  propagation](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/auto-instrumentation#trace-context-propagation).
- Approved rules for content capture, redaction, access control, and retention.
  Refer to [Privacy and content
  boundaries](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/auto-instrumentation#privacy-and-content-boundaries).

Use the deployment manifests and image versions supplied with your Agentic
Runtime Fabric distribution. Adapt addresses and service names to your
deployment.

## Enable inference gateway tracing

Inference gateway tracing is off by default. Enable it in the
`Observability.Tracing` block of the `inference-gateway` configuration entry.

| Field           | Description                                                        |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Enabled`       | Set to `true` to export traces.                                    |
| `OTLP.Endpoint` | The OpenTelemetry Protocol (OTLP) collector URL.                   |
| `OTLP.Insecure` | Sends OTLP without TLS when `true`. Use only in non-production environments. |
| `SampleRatio`   | Fraction of requests to trace, from `0` to `1`.                    |

When tracing is enabled, the gateway exports spans over OTLP and joins Envoy's
trace through the inbound `traceparent` header.

## Configure Envoy tracing

Configure the Envoy proxies on the observed paths to send network spans to the
collector. For example configurations, refer to [Distributed
tracing](/consul/docs/observe/distributed-tracing).

1. Add the collector cluster to the proxy bootstrap configuration with
   `envoy_extra_static_clusters_json`. Enable HTTP/2 on the cluster for OTLP
   over gRPC.
1. Configure the OpenTelemetry tracer with `envoy_tracing_json`. Set the service
   name and reference the collector cluster.

## Attach the payload processor

Attach the protocol-aware external processor that generates payload spans.

<!-- TODO: Confirm with engineering the SERVICE_NAME and OTLP_ENDPOINT settings and parser selection by bind-port group. None appear in consul, consul-enterprise, or consul-k8s at v2.1.0. -->

<!-- TODO: Confirm with engineering whether Envoy dials the MCP interceptor over the sidecar's Unix domain socket on Kubernetes. consul-enterprise v2.1.0+ent agent/xds/egress_mcp_endpoint.go:75-83 configures a loopback port, and consul-k8s v2.1.0 annotations_and_labels.go:286 says the sidecar listens on a UDS by default. -->

1. Attach the
   [`builtin/ext-proc`](/consul/docs/reference/proxy/extensions/ext-proc) Envoy
   extension to the observed outbound proxy listeners. Configure it to send
   request and response headers and bodies.
1. Configure buffered request and response bodies for the supported parsers,
   with explicit size limits.
1. Connect each processor to Envoy:
   - AI Inference Gateway: Envoy reaches the processor through the local
     `local_ext_proc` cluster. On Kubernetes, the processor listens on the Unix
     domain socket `/run/consul/ext_proc.sock`, shared with Envoy.
   - MCP sidecar: Envoy reaches the interceptor over loopback on port `21101` by
     default. To change the port, set `port` in the service's `interceptor`
     block. On Kubernetes, the sidecar listens on a Unix domain socket by
     default. To use TCP instead, set the `consul.hashicorp.com/ai-agent-addr`
     annotation to a port that matches the interceptor port.
1. Set `SERVICE_NAME` for the processor.
1. Set `OTLP_ENDPOINT` to the collector's OTLP over HTTP `/v1/traces` endpoint.
1. Match each observed upstream to its protocol parser. The reference
   implementation selects parsers by upstream bind-port group.

<Warning>

Keep the external-processing endpoint private. The loopback connection is
plaintext and relies on network-namespace isolation. On Kubernetes, the AI
Inference Gateway socket relies on file permissions instead, and Envoy must run
as the same user as the processor. Publishing either endpoint on a routable
interface exposes an unauthenticated payload reader.

</Warning>

## Start the components

Start the components in order, so no spans are lost while the collector starts.

1. Start the collector and the trace backend.
1. Apply the service and proxy configuration.
1. Start the sidecars and their processors. Recreate any proxy that is already
   running. Writing a new configuration entry does not replace a running
   proxy's bootstrap configuration.

## Verify spans reach the trace backend

Use synthetic, non-sensitive inputs for every step.

1. Send a sampled request through the entry point to an agent that makes one
   model call and one tool call.
1. Inspect the active proxy configuration. Confirm that it contains the
   OpenTelemetry tracer and the external-processing filter.
1. Confirm that the processor receives exchanges. A successful application
   response does not show that instrumentation works.
1. Confirm that the collector exports the spans to the trace backend. A
   collector acknowledgement does not show that the backend stored them.
1. Retrieve the trace by ID from the trace backend.
1. Confirm that network spans and payload spans share the trace context. Each
   payload span appears as a sibling of its Envoy egress span.
1. Confirm that payload spans carry the processor's service name, separate from
   the Envoy service name.
1. Confirm that the tool name, approved arguments, result, model information,
   and protocol errors match the synthetic request and response.
1. Confirm that the applications initialize no tracing SDK and emit no manual
   spans.
1. Confirm that the applications forward the trace context headers on
   downstream calls. Without them, the proxy spans do not form one workflow
   trace.
1. Test unsampled traffic, unsupported payloads, oversized bodies, and a
   collector outage. Check application behavior and telemetry-loss indicators.
